structured.approach: I followed the frontend-steps FE-04 procedure against the contracted inputs: task.components, feat.design B4, feat.stories STORY-07, feat.screens, org.design_library, org.lessons and org.engineering_stack. I read the current source with Read and with the CodeGraph MCP tool (codegraph_explore, projectPath set to the ap_portal checkout). The workbook action asks for proper comments. HTML_ESCAPES and DECIMAL_STRING had no comment, so I added a one-line `//` comment above each one. No behaviour changed. After the edit I ran codegraph sync and codegraph affected on src/ap_portal/index.js, then git status and the full CI (node ci.mjs). CodeGraph lists no affected tests because the tests import the module by package name. The code compiles, the 2 existing tests pass and there are no static issues. Only the coverage gate fails, and the owner deferred that gate to FE-05. I rewrote task.code.md in full with the new CI line and the new uncovered-line ranges. Its comments section now names each new constant and function. The version step stays an open question because package.json is outside this step's write scope.
tools_used: Bash (git status, git diff, node ci.mjs, codegraph status/sync/callers/impact/affected)

claims.text: src/ap_portal/index.js adds the constants RISK_CLASSES, OVERDUE_HEADINGS, HTML_ESCAPES and DECIMAL_STRING, the private helpers escapeHtml, toTwoDecimalString and riskClass, and the exported renderOverdueRisk. Each new constant and function has a `//` comment directly above it.

renderOverdueRisk returns '' for undefined, null or []. It throws TypeError for a non-array rows value or a non-integer days. Otherwise it renders table.overdue-risk with the header Invoice, Vendor, Days overdue, Amount, then one risk-* row per input row in the given order.
A row with risk high, medium, low or unknown gets the class risk-high, risk-medium, risk-low or risk-unknown. Any other risk value renders as risk-unknown.
Amounts are formatted only as strings and never go through Number(), parseFloat or formatAmount, in line with D-2026-044 and L-011.
HTML_ESCAPES, DECIMAL_STRING, escapeHtml and toTwoDecimalString each have 1 caller, inside src/ap_portal/index.js.
The existing exports VERSION, LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary are unchanged, and module.exports also exports renderOverdueRisk.
The component emits only class hooks, with no tokens or inline styles, because the design library defines no tokens for the risk classes.
CI sets passed only when line coverage is at least 90 and there are no static issues. The static checks flag console.log, eval( and lines longer than 140 characters.
The owner accepted FE-04 without the coverage gate. The new tests are written in FE-05, and the full CI, including the 90% gate, must pass before the commit step.
TK-07.5 asks for a package version step from 2.3.0 in both index.js and package.json. package.json still holds 2.3.0 and is outside this step's write scope, so the version step is deferred.
README.md and docs/ap_portal.md document renderOverdueRisk: signature, CT-1 input fields, output, errors, money and escaping rules, a synthetic example and the styling hooks.
The repository rule is to keep existing public signatures and add new functions for new behaviour.

open_questions: Q-1 (not blocking for FE-04; must be settled before FE-06): package.json is outside FE-04's write scope. Which step sets the next minor version in both src/ap_portal/index.js and package.json (DD-11, TK-07.5), and who confirms the number? Owner: Developer.
Q-2 (carried from CQ-FE-1): should a missing or non-string id or vendor throw TypeError, as days and amount do, instead of rendering String(value)? Owner: Architect.
Q-3 (carried from CQ-FE-2): who styles overdue-risk and the risk-* classes? The design library defines no tokens for them. Owner: UX lead.
structured.summary: STORY-07 is coded on feature/story in ap_portal and is not committed. src/ap_portal/index.js has renderOverdueRisk and its private helpers, built to feat.design B4, the AC-07 criteria in feat.stories and the FS-1/FS-2 frames in feat.screens. Each new constant and function now has a `//` comment; I added one above HTML_ESCAPES and one above DECIMAL_STRING. README.md and the new docs/ap_portal.md document the function. node ci.mjs reports compile true, 2 tests run, 0 failures, no static issues, coverage 60.32 and passed false. The only failure is the 90% coverage gate, which the owner moved to FE-05. task.code.md quotes the CI result and lists the tests FE-05 must add. The version step stays open as Q-1, and both files remain at 2.3.0.
